sentences.text: Pages No. 8/24 LOVLEEN 2023.05.12 tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as nonpecuniary damages.

The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The nonpecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment,
special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the nonpecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just'

(iii) Loss of actual earnings & Loss of future earnings 15.
In his affidavit Ex. PW3/A, the petitioner has failed to specify his vocation or profession.
Nor has he mentioned his income at the relevant time in his above affidavit.
During the course of final arguments Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has conceded that the monthly income of petitioner may be assessed as per minimum wages.

In the facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi as on the date of accident(petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi at the relevant time).
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to an unskilled person as on 13.09.2020 in Delhi were Rs. 14,842/.

Keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner would not have been able to resume his work/ vocation for a period of 04 months at least after the occurrence of the accident.
As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs. 59,368/ (Rs. 14,842 X 4).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under the head Loss of Actual Earnings.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The DAR was treated as a claim petition.
However,
R3/ Insurance Company declined to file a legal offer on the ground that at the relevant time R1 was driving the offending vehicle in a drunken condition.
None of the parties disputed the occurrence of the accident or the manner in which it took place nor the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
R3/ Insurance Company raised a sole objection to the effect that R1 was driving the offending vehicle in a drunken condition at the relevant time.
The said objection was rejected by this Tribunal vide order dated 12/09/2022 on the basis of observations made by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Manju Devi, 2014, SCC Online AP 232, by Karnataka High Court in National Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Mallikarjuna and Ors., MANU/KA/6179/2019 as well as The Divisional Manager National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Chinnamma and Ors., MANU/KA/5967/2019 and by Delhi High Court in Universal Sompo General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Vijay & Vicky and Anr in MAC.App. 678/2011 decided on 9th July, 2012.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
8. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
"Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?"
9. As the parties are not at issue regarding the fact that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to a road traffic accident involving the offending vehicle on account of the neglect and default of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time, therefore, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for injuries sustained by him in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
COMPENSATION Rahul Parcha vs Sanjay @ Sanju on 12 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107036919/
5 10.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as nonpecuniary damages.
The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The nonpecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment,
special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the nonpecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar &
Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
11.
It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which she actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.
1,00,000/ is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his MACT No. 297/21 Rahul Parcha Vs. Sanjay @ Sanju Ors.
Keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner would not have been able to resume his work/ vocation for a period of 04 months at least after the occurrence of the accident.
However, the petitioner has not been able to prove the nature of his vocation/ job and therefore, the monthly income of the petitioner has been assumed as per minimum wages admissible to an unskilled person.
In the absence of any material to the contrary, it would be appropriate to assume that the earning capacity of petitioner stands reduced by 12.5% (half of the actual physical disability).
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
As already stated above, R-1 being the driver and principal tortfeasor and R-2 being owner of the offending vehicle, and also being vicariously liable for the acts of R-1, are jointly and severally liable to pay the awarded amount of compensation to petitioners.

opennyai_summary.decision:
SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '16' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.
The petitioner is also entitled to future prospects as per the MACT No. 297/21 Rahul Parcha Vs. Sanjay @ Sanju Ors.
Thus, the loss of future earnings of petitioner due to him above injury and permanent disability comes to Rs. 4,98,691/ (rounded off) (Rs. 14,842/ X 12.5/100 X 140/100 X 16 X 12) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under the head 'Loss of Future Income'.
Petitioner claims he incurred expenses to the tune of Rs. 400/ to Rs. 800/ towards conveyance for each follow up/ consultation visit after his discharge from the hospital.

the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs. 10,000/ each under these heads.
